scope: Theorem 13.1 (Effective simulation with explicit bounds) of the manuscript “Exact derandomization of logarithmic space: L = RL = BPL” (preprints/Exact-Derandomization-of-Logarithmic-Space-L-equals-RL-equals-BPL-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 103 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 15030fab23d31a4d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 98. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is a terminating algorithm which, given a finite randomized machine description M and positive integers a, b, emits a deterministic machine DM and positive integers K, H, c with the following guarantee. If, on every input of length n and every random tape, M halts within (n + 2)a steps, uses at most b⌈log(n + 2)⌉ work bits, and has acceptance probability at most 1/3 on no inputs and at least 2/3 on yes inputs, then DM decides the same language. On each input, that same execution uses at most K log(n + 2) work bits and H(n + 2)c elementary bit operations.
